messages:
Ethan Li: Hey team — kicking off a staged rollout plan for structured-output / function-calling compatibility. Goal: enable the new structured responses for canary audiences while keeping default SDK behavior unchanged. Draft plan + quick checks below, please ack and call out blockers. :party-blob:

Priya Desai: thanks Ethan — can you list the exact feature-flag keys, audiences, and the expected client behaviour differences? also who owns the console toggle entry?

Ethan Li: sure. flags: `compat_structured_output_v1` (server-side), and `sdk_fncall_compat_v2` (client SDK opt-in). Initial audiences: 1) internal (@redwood), 2) 5 selected PLG customers (IDs shared in the sheet), 3) 5% randomized traffic in Hosted API after internal/PLG. Expected behaviour: default SDKs remain unchanged. When `sdk_fncall_compat_v2=true`, SDK will accept and surface `structured` responses (JSON payload in `response.structured`). When server `compat_structured_output_v1=true`, runtime will emit structured blocks alongside legacy text in debug mode for the canary (see below).

Jordan Patel: runtime notes: we should avoid sending two full token streams on prod due to cost. For canary we can include `structured_preview` (small JSON pointer + hash) rather than full duplicate tokens. If SDK requests full structured output, route to a structured-enabled model variant. Need to ensure KV cache and quantization paths support the variant without latency cliff. I can add a runtime guard to reject requests > max_len in structured mode to prevent tail blowups.

Samira Khan: devex asks: update quickstart + changelog and add migration snippet. Also add telemetry event `compat_structured.enabled` with fields: sdk_version, user_id, flag_source. Will update the SDK README.

Maya Rivera: QA plan (high level): 1) unit tests for parser fallback, 2) e2e with sample function schema sets (10 examples), 3) smoke on dedicated nodes, 4) chaos/rollback test flipping flag mid-session. We need test customers consent simulation for PLG ones.

Oliver Huang: schedule proposal: canary ramp: internal 0h -> 24h, PLG cohort for 48h, then randomized 5% for 72h, 25% for 48h, full ramp after metrics green. Preconditions for ramp: no increase in 5xx > x2 baseline, p95 latency < +30%, structured parse-error rate < 0.5%, no regressions in core templates. Who owns go/no-go?

Ethan Li: I'll own go/no-go with Priya + Maya. Rollback plan: 1) flip server flag off via console (instant), 2) revert SDK publish (if needed) and notify customers. We'll keep a hotfix branch ready for runtime patch.

Alex Kim: CS note — some enterprise customers require explicit opt-in in contract. Please surface a per-customer allowlist toggle and an audit message when enabled.

Priya Desai: noted — console will have per-customer scope for the flag and audit logging. I'll create the toggle entry and add owner tags. ETA: I'll add it to the console this afternoon.

Ethan Li: internal checklist (short):
- [x] flag keys decided: `compat_structured_output_v1`, `sdk_fncall_compat_v2`
- [x] PRs opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/311
- [ ] console toggle created (Priya)
- [ ] telemetry events merged (Samira)
- [ ] QA tests green (Maya)
- [ ] canary customer emails prepped (Alex)

Jordan Patel: added runtime PR comment: add `structured_preview` header when full duplication is disabled. Also tag ops to ensure GPU pool autoscale policy doesn't throttle canary.

Samira Khan: SDK snippet for customers who opt in (I'll include in README):
```js
// opt into function-calling compat v2
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, flags: { sdk_fncall_compat_v2: true } });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-structured-1', input: '...' });
console.log(res.structured); // JSON output
```

Maya Rivera: QA quick checklist to run before PLG cohort:
- run parser fallback test harness (10k msgs)
- check error codes mapping (no new 4xx/5xx types)
- validate structured schema conformance on 20 sample schemas
- smoke test on Dedicated with quantized model variants

Oliver Huang: I'll schedule the canary windows in the release calendar. Need owners to add pre/post checks to the deploy runbook. Also add a postmortem template in case we need to roll back.

Ethan Li: metrics to watch (live dashboard):
- structured_parse_error_rate (per-model)
- p95 latency change (per-audience)
- 5xx rate
- per-customer complaint tickets
- token usage delta (cost)
- SDK telemetry opt-ins

Priya Desai: console update done — toggle `compat_structured_output_v1` created with scopes: `global`, `customer.allowlist`, `internal`. Owner=eng-platform. Audit log enabled.

CI Bot: Deploy bot: `staged-rollout/compat-structured` pipeline started for internal canary at 1823457010 — status: started

Samira Khan: I merged telemetry PR, event naming `compat_structured.enabled` + `compat_structured.fallback_used`. SDKs will send anonymized schema hashes.

Ethan Li: final ask before we flip internal: any last concerns about client SDK surface? specifically — will mobile SDK behavior differ? (iOS/Android)

Alex Kim: mobile SDK teams will need a small update; we should coordinate a minor SDK release and call out changes in the migration guide. Customers on pinned SDKs won't see changes until they opt in, so low risk.

Priya Desai: ready on console side. I added an allowlist entry for the 5 PLG test customers (IDs in the sheet).

Maya Rivera: starting QA runs now. Will post results in ~4h.

Ethan Li: thanks everyone — I'll flip internal canary at 1823457100, monitor the dashboard for 24h, then follow the ramp plan. Please react with :thumbsup: when you see this if you're good.
